svg.title: From ESXi VM to guest OS on KubeVirt: layers and owners
svg.desc: Vertical chain: ESXi VM, KubeVirt VirtualMachine, VirtualMachineInstance, virt-launcher Pod, QEMU, KVM, guest OS, with the component that owns each layer.
svg.text: The chain from an ESXi VM to a running guest on KubeVirt
ESXi VM (source)
.vmx config + .vmdk disks on a VMFS datastore
runs as a VMX process on VMkernel
Owner: ESXi (hostd, VMkernel)
Leaves the picture after migration. The platform reads
its metadata and copies its disks; it does not run it.
migration: translate metadata, convert + import disks
VirtualMachine (kubevirt.io/v1)
persistent desired state: CPU, memory, disks, NICs
spec.runStrategy decides whether it should be running
Owner: you (kubectl / GitOps / migration controller)
Survives stop/start. Like a StatefulSet with replicas=1.
virt-api validates it; virt-controller acts on it.
virt-controller creates VMI when runStrategy says run
VirtualMachineInstance (VMI)
one running instance; deleted when the VM stops
status: phase, nodeName, interfaces, guest info
Owner: virt-controller (ownerReference to the VM)
Ephemeral, like a Pod. Recreated from the VM template.
virt-handler takes over once nodeName is set.
virt-controller creates the launcher Pod; scheduler places it
virt-launcher Pod (virt-launcher-<vm>-xxxxx)
compute container: virt-launcher + libvirt + QEMU
gets the pod IP, mounted PVCs, CPU/memory limits
Owners: kube-scheduler (placement), kubelet (runs it)
Kubernetes treats it as a normal Pod: cgroups, namespaces,
CNI networking, CSI volume mounts.
virt-handler (node) tells virt-launcher to start the domain
QEMU process (the VM's user-space process)
emulates machine + virtio devices; vCPUs are threads
disk = PVC (file disk.img or raw block device)
Owner: libvirt inside virt-launcher (domain XML)
Runs inside the Pod's cgroup, so Pod requests/limits
apply to the VM. Comparable to the VMX process on ESXi.
ioctl() on /dev/kvm: create VM, vCPUs, memory slots
KVM (kernel module on the node)
VT-x/AMD-V: guest code runs directly on the CPU
EPT/NPT: guest-physical to host-physical memory
Owner: node Linux kernel
Exposed to the Pod as the /dev/kvm device (virt-handler
advertises it). Comparable to the VMM in VMkernel.
Guest OS + application (e.g. Linux + nginx)
the same OS that ran on ESXi, now on virtio devices
Owner: application / OS team
Kubernetes cannot see processes inside the guest; it only
sees the Pod. Guest health needs probes or the guest agent.
